title: Looking Back on First Year
subtitle: First year of Computer Engineering
paragraphs: Going into first year at the University of Guelph, I wanted to do well academically, get involved in engineering clubs, meet people, and build a foundation for the rest of my degree.
I made an effort to get to know other students, professors, and people working in engineering, rather than spending all my time focused on coursework.

Throughout the year, I got involved with IEEE, attended hackathons and engineering competitions, and continued working on my own hardware and software projects. Those experiences taught me a lot about working with teams and applying technical skills.
I maintained a GPA in the high 3.0s, which I was happy with. It mattered to me to do well in class while still leaving time to build things and take part in opportunities outside university.

I’ve come to appreciate that balance. Good grades are valuable, and so is having something to show for what you’re learning. I’m satisfied with how first year went and the connections I made along the way.
